principles.statement: When duplicates of a logical entity exist, resolve the canonical one by a stable, order-independent key — minimum container id — never by iteration order.
principles.rationale: Live-confirmed 2026-09-20 twice: root 7 held 41 scope codes duplicated up to 8x; 'insert into map' resolved to the NEWEST duplicate each boot (edges scattered, count never converged), and 'first occurrence in child_ids' broke when the storage layer reshuffled child_ids across restarts (wired 27 then 30 on consecutive boots).

principles.statement: A boot-time idempotency claim is only proven when the wired/created count converges to zero across real restarts — the unit-test guarantee does not survive an unstable input ordering.
principles.rationale: The T-J5 idempotency test passed while live boots kept wiring fresh scaffolds, because the test's input order was stable and production's was not.

principles.statement: Data-integrity bugs announce themselves as counts that drift: identical data producing different totals across runs.
principles.rationale: 'Jurisdiction graph: wired 27/35/24/21 relationship edges' across boots on unchanged files was the entire bug report — the varying number WAS the finding.

heuristics.name: Building a name/scope -> container-id map over children that may contain historical duplicates.
heuristics.description: Keep the MINIMUM container id per key (entry().and_modify with a min-compare). Insertion order, hash order, and reload order all lie; ids don't.
heuristics.when_to_apply: Any boot-time or query-time resolution over a graph with possible duplicates.

heuristics.name: A convergence count (wired/registered/repaired) does not reach zero on the second identical run.
heuristics.description: Stop adding special cases; dump the full set of targets, diff them across two runs, and find what is unstable before touching the algorithm again.

decision_rules.condition: Wiring or updating entities resolved through a container map.
decision_rules.action: Resolve canonically by min-id first; verify the second identical run performs zero writes before considering the feature done.
